{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABajcmDA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhEKAtc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 73, "title": "Implement VDP1 HDTV/31 kHz mode and exclusive-monitor sprite composition", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `c94d5c4ea5bf18c0185f5e9f5a04ecabdfe5de65`, `Vdp1::validate_write` rejects TVMR.TVM=4, a documented HDTV/31 kHz mode. VDP2 already supports exclusive-monitor outputs, but their existing guest tests exercise backgrounds rather than this missing VDP1 path.

Allowing the register value alone is insufficient. `Vdp2::sprite_data` currently uses unscaled X and only halves Y for double-density interlace. Also, `Vdp1::vblank_out` permits display-period erase when TVM=4 because its exclusion mask omits that bit. These paths must implement the mode's actual readout and erase behavior.

This is a focused missing video programming mode under #17, building on the existing raster, framebuffer, transaction and composition implementations.

## Expected outcome

Implement functional VDP1 HDTV/31 kHz operation through real guest commands, framebuffer memory and VDP2 composition.

The primary contract is:

- VDP1 TVM=4 uses a 512×256, 16-bit framebuffer and noninterlaced operation. Encodings 5–7 remain prohibited. See Sega VDP1 User's Manual §4.1, table 4.2, and its setting-window requirements. [Primary reference](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p04_11.htm)
- VDP1 supplies a 320×240 or 352×240 source image in exclusive-monitor operation. Its documented physical output repeats each source color over a 2×2 block. Derive the mapping to each exposed VDP2 output resolution explicitly; do not enlarge framebuffer storage or invoke the rotation-background matrix. See VDP1 §1.2, table 1.2. [Primary reference](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p01_20.htm)
- HDTV framebuffer erase occurs during VBlank, including with VBE clear, rather than during display. Preserve captured erase operands, partial completion and blank-end cancellation. VDP1 §4.4, tables 4.4–4.5 give capacities of 29,340 pixels for 31 kHz and 53,136 for HDTV. [Primary reference](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p04_14.htm)
- Compose sprites with the existing four exclusive VDP2 modes, respecting their documented restrictions and background multiplexing. See VDP2 §2.1, table 2.1 and exclusive high-resolution settings. [Primary reference](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p02_10.htm)

Keep unspecified publication phases identified as emulator conventions. Reconcile applicable primary corrections before implementation. Evidence-backed corrections to this AI-authored task should update the Issue with exact references and rationale; they require no human approval.

Scope excludes unrelated raster half-line work, general rasterizer refinements and other chip conformance.

## Context and reproduction

Read-only inspection establishes the missing behavior:

1. `src/vdp1.rs:281–294` accepts only TVM=0–3; writing TVMR=4 returns `UnsupportedDevice`.
2. `src/vdp2/rotation.rs:117–126` has no exclusive-monitor sprite coordinate mapping.
3. `src/vdp1.rs:357–363` does not suppress display erase for HDTV, although `hblank_in` already recognizes its automatic blank-erase requirement.
4. `tests/video_transactions.rs:242–267` covers exclusive-monitor dimensions, counters and background pixels, without enabling TVM=4.

Use the existing `videoTransactions` browser scenario and original fixture infrastructure where practical. No personal firmware, commercial discs or physical monitor is needed.

The supplied main CI snapshot has native/Wasm jobs in progress; these are pending observations, not failures or passing acceptance. Planning did not rerun complete suites.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document a primary-derived table covering valid TVMR values, framebuffer geometry, sprite coordinate mapping, legal mode-setting windows and erase behavior. Separate hardware requirements from phase conventions.
- [ ] Add independent native tests proving TVM=4 succeeds through scheduled SH-2 MMIO, MODR reports its written setting, framebuffer addressing remains 512×256×16 bits, and prohibited encodings remain diagnosed. Exercise both SH-2 access paths and preserve existing transaction-width behavior.
- [ ] Verify literal sprite pixels in all four exclusive VDP2 outputs: 320/352/640/704×480. Use distinct neighboring source pixels and rows, including source row 239 and the rightmost visible column, to detect missing repetition, incorrect scaling, wrapping and bottom-half transparency. Include RGB555 and palette sprites, transparency and valid priority overlap with backgrounds.
- [ ] Verify HDTV performs no display-period erase and automatically performs VBlank erase with VBE=0. Use independently derived capacities `(852−200)×(525−480)=29340` and `(848−200)×(562−480)=53136`; assert the last completed word and first untouched word in an unsaturated rectangle, retained operands/destination, interruption at blank end and no duplicate display erase. Preserve the established sampled-VBE contract for existing modes.
- [ ] Cover automatic/manual framebuffer changes, PTMR starts, END/status/draw-end IRQ, legal transitions into and out of TVM=4, reset cancellation, advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and passive inspection without changing results. Do not assign hardware guarantees to prohibited register-write windows.
- [ ] Add or extend an original MIT-licensed synthetic BIOS guest that draws through VDP1 commands, selects the exclusive modes, computes framebuffer/status/IRQ records and supplies actual composed pixels. Run identical bytes in native Machine tests and production browser Wasm under `/saturn-rust/`, checking Canvas pixels, changed color/coordinate operands, omitted-draw controls and repeated cold boots. Register reproducible source, bytes and hashes. Demonstrate inherited-code rejection; accepting TVMR=4 alone must not satisfy the pixel or erase oracles.
- [ ] Preserve Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, standard-TV sprites, rotation, interlace, VBE/erase capture, DMA/bus ownership, sound, backup, input and privacy regressions. Update architecture, conformance and validation records with exact implementation/test/spec links and remaining deviations.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native and Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, existing runner regressions and the complete `npm run test:browser` inventory. Retain the existing CI coverage and publication gates without skipped required scenarios.

This resolves only the scoped VDP1 mode increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral semantics, multiprocessor synchronization, bus/cache/reset/arbitration, SCU/DSP, video/audio/CD timing and behavior, media/HLE/SMPC services and comprehensive integration evidence remain mandatory under #17. Genuine BIOS operation and broad commercial-game compatibility remain unverified. No umbrella completion criterion is satisfied merely by this task's merge.

## Optional validation

None required beyond the automated acceptance above.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
